title: The Geometry of Knowledge Accessibility in Large Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.03052v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) contain broad knowledge, but they cannot access all of it reliably. We study this problem through knowledge accessibility, which describes whether the knowledge needed for a query can be recalled from the model. We find that knowledge accessibility has a simple geometric structure in the model's representation of the query alone, before any generation. More accessible queries are closer to a center in the representation space, while less accessible queries are farther away. This geometry reveals a knowledge boundary that separates more accessible queries from less accessible ones. Accessibility consistently decreases with distance from the center, and this distance-based ordering transfers across datasets even when the centers differ. translated_title: 大语言模型中知识可及性的几何结构
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLMs）包含广泛的知识，但它们无法可靠地访问所有这些知识。我们通过“知识可及性”来研究这一问题，即查询所需的知识能否从模型中被回忆起来。我们发现，在模型生成任何内容之前，仅从模型对查询本身的表示中，知识可及性就呈现出一种简单的几何结构：越容易被访问的查询在表示空间中越靠近某个中心，而越难被访问的查询则离中心越远。这种几何结构揭示了一条知识边界，将更易访问的查询与较难访问的查询区分开来。可及性随离中心距离的增加而持续下降，并且这种基于距离的排序即使在不同中心的情况下也能跨数据集迁移。受控实验进一步表明，这种以中心为核心的几何结构与知识可及性的关联比与推理难度的关联更为紧密。该几何结构还揭示了……
tldr: 大语言模型的知识可及性在查询的表示空间中呈现出以中心为参照的几何结构——查询表示离中心越近其所需知识越容易被召回，由此可以在生成之前就通过几何距离刻画并预测模型的知识边界。
en_tdlr: Knowledge accessibility in LLMs exhibits a center-based geometric structure in query representations—queries closer to the center are more accessible—enabling the model's knowledge boundary to be characterized and predicted from query embeddings before any generation.
